scores.evidence: Phase 2 "Depends on: Phase 1, and the labeled question set." Phase 3 "Depends on: V4."
scores.rationale: Phases build upward with explicit dependencies and gates, and later work is not specified until earlier work is validated.

scores.evidence: "A staff member asks in the live help-center widget... The answer streams back and cites the password-reset article."
scores.rationale: Phase 0 is a real end-to-end production slice (widget, API, retrieval, LLM, trace) with deploy, rollback and a V0 gate.

scores.evidence: Tradeoff table: "Decision | Reversibility | Default | Assumption | Validated by | Flip condition"
scores.rationale: Irreversible decisions are listed up front with defaults, reversibility ratings, assumptions and explicit flip conditions.

scores.evidence: Phase 1 lists the indexing filter and personal-data removal first, then the output renderer, then filters, caps and the handoff tool.
scores.rationale: Within each phase, the widest-impact items (data boundary, index filter, rebuild/ingest) come before leaf items, though the ordering is implicit rather than argued.

scores.evidence: Phase 0: "Secrets in a vault; staff-only flag; user and retrieved text passed as data; outbound traffic only to the LLM provider"
scores.rationale: The cross-cutting table gives concrete security treatment in every phase, starting at Phase 0.

scores.evidence: "One OpenTelemetry trace covers widget → API → retrieval → LLM. Metrics for latency, tokens, cost and errors."
scores.rationale: Observability is in Phase 0 and each later phase has concrete items (dashboards, freshness metrics, faithfulness sampling).

scores.evidence: "Model ID, prompt version and index version live in versioned config and are stamped on every trace."
scores.rationale: Versioned config, IaC, versioned indexes, pinned models and logged experiment assignments appear in every phase.

scores.evidence: Phase 0: "Timeout falls back to search; flag works as a kill switch"; the V0 test revokes the LLM key to inject a failure
scores.rationale: Failure handling is concrete in every phase, with fallbacks, alias rollback, a fallback model and auto-rollback.

scores.evidence: "Phase 1 — Defenses and budgets" precedes "Phase 2 — Retrieval" and "Phase 3 — Model access, memory, orchestration"; routing is marked not needed
scores.rationale: The order is defenses, budgets and human-in-the-loop, then retrieval, model access, memory, orchestration, routing (deferred) and feedback, which is correct.

scores.evidence: "Model routing... when cost per resolution misses the V6 target while a cheaper model still passes V5."
scores.rationale: The deferred list is explicit, and each item has a pull-forward condition.

note: This is a very strong plan. It has a real Phase 0 skeleton, gates, threaded concerns and correct AI layer ordering. I found no significant gaps.
